title: Discounting an Interest-Bearing Note before Maturity

cards.front: What does it mean to [[kw:discount a note]]?
back: Selling a promissory note to a bank before its maturity date to obtain cash earlier.
The bank charges a fee ([[kw:bank discount]]) and gives the company the [[kw:proceeds]].
[[imp:Discounting does not eliminate the company's liability if the maker defaults.]]
A potential obligation that arises if the original maker of a discounted note fails to pay.
The company that discounted the note remains responsible to pay the bank the maturity value.
It is removed only when the maker pays the note at maturity.
1. Find the interest and [[kw:maturity value]] (MV) of the original note.
2. Determine the [[kw:discount period]] (days from discount date to maturity).
3. Calculate the [[kw:bank discount]] on the maturity value for the discount period.
4. Compute [[kw:proceeds]] = MV - Bank discount.
cards.front: List the four steps of discounting a note.

back: $$I = \text{Face Value} \times \text{Note Rate} \times \frac{\text{Full Term}}{360}$$
$$MV = \text{Face Value} + I$$
This is the amount the bank will collect at maturity.
cards.front: How do you calculate the maturity value of a discounted note?

back: The number of days from the discount date (when the bank buys the note) to the maturity date.
It is the time the bank holds the note.
[[imp:It is not the full term of the note.]]

cards.front: How do you calculate the bank discount?
back: $$\text{Bank Discount} = MV \times \text{Discount Rate} \times \frac{\text{Discount Period}}{360}$$
The bank discount is the fee the bank charges for discounting the note.
It is computed on the maturity value, not the face value.

cards.front: How do you find the proceeds from discounting?
back: $$\text{Proceeds} = MV - \text{Bank Discount}$$
Proceeds are the cash the company receives from the bank.
Always less than the maturity value.
The discounter must pay the bank the full maturity value.
The contingent liability becomes an actual liability.
The discounter's net loss = MV - Proceeds (which equals the bank discount).
cards.front: If the maker of a discounted note defaults, what must the discounter do?
A $2,000, 8% note for 90 days is discounted after 30 days at 6%. Find the proceeds.
back: Step 2: Discount period = 90 - 30 = 60 days.
Step 3: Bank discount = 2,040 x 0.06 x 60/360 = $20.40.

cards.front: Why is the bank discount calculated on the maturity value rather than the face value?
back: Because the bank will collect the full maturity value at the note's due date.
The bank's return is based on that future amount, not the original principal.
Using MV ensures the bank earns its discount on the amount it is advancing.

cards.front: What happens if the maker pays the note at maturity after it has been discounted?
back: The bank receives the maturity value directly from the maker.
The discounter's contingent liability is removed.
The discounter keeps the proceeds and has no further obligation.
1. Understand: list face value, note rate, full term, discount date, discount rate.
2. Solve: follow the four steps (MV, discount period, bank discount, proceeds).
3. Conclude: check that proceeds < MV, state proceeds and contingent liability.
